The seed_data management command creates demo users with hard-coded passwords ('adminpass', 'clinicianpass', 'frontdeskpass', 'patientpass') that are also published in README.md. These identical passwords work across multiple accounts. If the seed command is run in production, the database is populated with weak, predictable credentials that any authenticated insider or leaked credential can use.

The _wrk_gate() auth check at lines 19-21 reads the internal API token from os.environ.get('INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN'). If this environment variable is not set, gate_value is None and bool(None) is False, meaning _wrk_gate() always returns False and all ops endpoints return 403. This is a security misconfiguration where the auth check can silently fail to enforce. In a misconfigured deployment where the env var is accidentally empty string, all endpoints are blocked unnecessarily. If the token is ever leaked from source or memory, it protects nothing since there is no secondary auth layer.

The document_upload endpoint at line 637-639 allows any staff user (not just assigned clinicians) to select an arbitrary patient via the GET 'patient' parameter, then upload documents on behalf of that patient. Lines 638-639 fetch PatientProfile via get_object_or_404 without verifying the staff user's relationship to the patient. Combined with the mass assignment in import_appointments, this creates a comprehensive access-control gap.
